blockers.description: CR-01: shadow silence is tracked account-wide (monitoringHealth.ts:141 holds one lastShadowMessageAt) while telemetry ownership is per device, and onReportedPatch discards the deviceId it is handed (accountRuntime.ts:613,639). On a two-pump account one pump's heartbeat re-stamps the account clock, so a permanently quiet pump never trips shadowSilent, is never released, and has every poll body discarded. Reproduced over 10 simulated hours: poll reported 31 on all 40 polls, store still read 3, Status Active stayed true.

CR-02: a control press after a credential refusal permanently un-marks both controls. refuseLocally -> armClearingPush -> clearRefusal -> republish() -> publishRow ends in publishValue(service, StatusActive, ...), and a value push clears a stored status. Permanent, because a halted runtime never pushes again. expire() and refuseOutcome() leak identically.
blockers.workaround: the restored-accessory path does not leak because it passes nothingToRepublish — that is the shape of the fix

blockers.description: CR-03: a metadata-only shadow document steals telemetry ownership. carriesObservation answers `data || state`, but ownership governs `data` alone, so a state-only update/accepted delta establishes the watermark having delivered no telemetry.
CR-04: README.md:145 and CHANGELOG.md:24 promise readings the code discards for ~30 minutes before release; test/runtime/accountRuntime.test.ts:987 pins the opposite behaviour deliberately.
The Cucumber suite has NO multi-device coverage — every scenario uses a single deviceId. That is the sole reason CR-01 survived twelve rounds of per-plan verification.
blockers.workaround: add multi-device scenarios as a deliverable in their own right

decisions.decision: Phase 5 executes on a new branch features/phase-05-degraded-operation-and-recovery cut from current HEAD, not origin/main
decisions.rationale: origin/main is 405 commits behind and contains no Phase 3 or Phase 4 source; the configured branching strategy would have built Phase 5 on nothing

decisions.decision: A REST-only degradation withdraws the connectivity scope and only that scope (D-02 over D-04)
decisions.rationale: D-02 is the later text, written specifically to fix a connectivity defect; a frozen offlineCount reading as trustworthy while REST is down is the false normal the project exists to prevent

decisions.decision: Two missed heartbeats release the shadow's ownership of telemetry (new D-13, amending D-15 and SYNC-03)
decisions.rationale: pollTelemetry froze telemetry during silence because releaseShadowSource had one caller, handleShadowDisconnected, and silence is not a disconnection. Proven: a flooded poll read 0 during silence and 31 after release.

decisions.decision: No ADR amendment or checkpoint was needed for D-014 when fixing CR-01
decisions.rationale: D-014 mandates no withholding; withholding is how retain is achieved when the arriving value is bad, and it retains nothing when a working transport delivered a family-valid value. 05-CONTEXT D-02 says so in its own words and its narrowing note already named toRow returning [] as a defect.

decisions.decision: WR-02 / SC-3's restored-switch press window was closed rather than honouring 05-04's PA-08 deferral
decisions.rationale: RES-04's clause opens 'After a failed restart', which is that window; reading it to govern only routable commands would make requirement scope depend on implementation completeness

decisions.decision: Fix the credential-persistence gap and then re-review the whole phase, rather than fixing narrowly
decisions.rationale: Maintainer ruling. Only the first five plans had ever been code-reviewed, and the gap round changed trust semantics, telemetry ownership, the auth halt path and the restore path.

decisions.decision: CR-01's marking stays account-wide; only telemetry ownership and arrival stamps become per-device
decisions.rationale: No requirement asks for per-device marking, D-02 already ratifies marking every accessory, and over-marking cannot produce a false normal. Per-device marking would push a per-device MonitoringTrust through onMonitoringHealth, applyMonitoringHealth and every trust literal in the unit suite — a second design change riding on the blocker. Recorded as a ledger todo.

decisions.decision: CR-02 is fixed by guarding the republish seam, not by teaching publishRow to push the persistent failure
decisions.rationale: The review's first option would add a second production call site of the act 03-CONTEXT.md D-05 forbids, and publishPersistentFailure's docblock says the single call site is what keeps that locked decision reviewable. One seam guard closes refuseLocally, expire and refuseOutcome together — the shape bindRestoredControlRefusal already demonstrates by not leaking.

context_notes: Phase 5 has run 12 plans across 78 commits, two full review rounds and two verification rounds, moving 1/4 -> 3/4 success criteria. Suite grew 1207->1349 unit tests and 78->96 scenarios at 100/100/100 coverage throughout. The phase's defining lesson, seen eleven times: a check passes because the thing it rests on already sits at the value the defect produces. It appeared in fixtures, harnesses, tooling, plans, and finally between plans — three of the four outstanding blockers are interactions that per-plan verification structurally cannot see. Executors repeatedly disproved premises their own plans asserted, which is the behaviour to keep encouraging.
